chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from Salih ibn Uqba, from Yunus ibn Zabyan who said:
He (peace be upon him) said to me: 'O Yunus! Do not swear an oath by disavowing from us, for whoever swears by disavowing from us, truthfully or falsely, he has indeed been disavowed from us.'

key_terms.البراءة: Disavowal, renunciation, severing of ties — the opposite of walaya (allegiance). In Shia theology, bara'a from the enemies of the Ahl al-Bayt is a duty, but here it refers to swearing that one disavows the Imams themselves.
key_terms.بَرِئَ: He was/became disavowed, cut off, separated — the consequence for the one who swears this forbidden oath.
key_terms.حلف: To swear an oath, to take a solemn vow. In Islamic law, oaths invoke God's name or sacred concepts as guarantors.

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about swearing an oath by disavowing from the Ahl al-Bayt?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) forbade his companion Yunus ibn Zabyan from swearing oaths in which one disavows or renounces connection to the Ahl al-Bayt. The ruling is categorical: whether such an oath is sworn truthfully (meaning the person genuinely believes they are not aligned with the Imams) or falsely (as a social convention or under pressure), the consequence is the same — the one who swears it is spiritually cut off from the Imams. This reflects the profound theological and legal importance of maintaining one's allegiance (walaya) to the Ahl al-Bayt in Shia doctrine.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Al Husayn, from Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Salih Bin Uqba, from Yunus Bin Zabyan who said,

‘He<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘O Yunus! Do not swear an oath with the disavowing (giving up/rejecting) from us<sup>asws</sup>, for the one who swear with the disavowing from us<sup>asws</sup>, truly or falsely, so he is disavowed (rejected) from us<sup>asws</sup>’.
en.sarwar: 2. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Muhammad ibn ’Isma‘il from Salih ibn ‘Uqbah from Yunus ibn Zabayan who has narrated the following: “He (the Imam), ‘Alayhi al-Salam, said to me, ‘O Yunus, do not swear to disown us, because if one does so, true or false, he is cut off from us.’”
